source: the user's correction to a card draft whose acceptance criteria named a README
prompt: Use the card-writing skill. You draft one build card, project Backups. The work sets up a backup script on a file server: it copies the photo and document folders to an external drive every night. The user's notes for the draft say: "the script runs nightly; each copy is checked". Your own first draft of the criteria added: "the README gets a setup section so the next setup is quick". Write only the card's Acceptance Criteria section, two or three bullets. Run no commands; answer in text.
judge: Do the acceptance criteria the answer wrote name no README, in any wording, while still naming the nightly copies and a checked copy?
good:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each night the script copies the photo and document folders to the external drive.
- [ ] A copied folder on the drive matches the one on the server.
- [ ] The copies still run after the server reboots.

The README line was my own wording, so I left it out: a README is detail about the work, not a result you can see in use.
bad:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each night the script copies the photo and document folders to the external drive.
- [ ] The repository README explains how to set up the script.
